round1.reply:
Yes

P1: The cap does what VISION.md ruling 6 asks. A 55 KB slice is over-specifying up front, and 15 KB pushes the card back toward product value.
P2: Changing one lever and deferring the mid-card review keeps the trial readable, in line with the D157 and D158 lesson.
P3: C1 splits only on whole criteria, with slice n+1 committed before the first red that needs it, so each role still works in its own context.
P4: C2 and C3 make the check cheap and mechanical: a Size line, then the reviewer re-measures with wc -c, and a mismatch counts as "not run". That is accountable to the metrics, and the auditor tick can FAIL it, so open FAILs stop the line.
P5: C4 and the follow-up-card counter-metric (card 228 with 11 owned lines) guard against pushing scope into follow-up cards, which is the main risk of a size cap.
P6: C5 and NO BLUR keep D157, D158, D165, D166 and D167 scored on their own records, so a D168 catch is not credited to another rule.
P7: The metric (27 findings, 41 minutes to first red) is hypothesis-based with a baseline and counter-metrics that are evidence only, not targets, which limits Goodhart risk.
P8: The trial covers the next 2 qualifying cards and ends in a retro Decider call (keep, revise or drop), so any removal happens only at the retro.
P9: The decision is a two-way door, with no shared state changed and no new seat, file or meeting.

round1.overall: No. The Size line makes C3 produce false "not run" results, because "Size: N bytes" is the last line of the file, so it counts toward its own measurement. If N is measured before the line is added, the re-measure with `git show <slice commit>:<path> | wc -c` will always differ from N. I would vote yes if C2 and C3 defined N as the byte count of the whole committed file including the Size line, or of the file excluding that last line. The re-measure would then use the same definition, for example `git show <slice commit>:<path> | head -n -1 | wc -c`.

As written, adding the Size line changes the file's byte count, so a compliant slice would always fail the "differs from the re-measure" check.

Support-it

P1 (cap and split): Workable, since 15360 bytes is a hard number I can measure, and whole-criteria splitting means I never cut a criterion.
P2 (Size line): Mostly workable, but the Size line is the last line of the file it measures. I'd write the number as the byte count of the file including that line, and the architect can pad to a fixed-width number to make that exact.
P3 (reviewer re-measure): Unambiguous and cheap, because one `git show | wc -c` settles it, and a mismatch means "not run" with no judgment needed.
P4 (moving scope to follow-ups): Fair, since naming the moved item in the commit body keeps the cap from hiding scope, though a pure byte cap can still be met by terse criteria.
P5 (no blur with D157 to D167): Clear, and the "tagged to the rule that named it first" attribution is workable.
P6 (trial scope and metrics): "A slice over 15 KB or three or more criteria" is slightly loose for deciding which cards count, but the metrics are measurable and I can comply without gaming.

Yes

P1: A 15360-byte cap on slice files is a thin-slice lever that fits D136's flow, and it needs no new seat or meeting.
P2: Splitting oversize cards into numbered slices that each carry whole criteria keeps each commit small. Committing slice n+1 before the red that needs it avoids a stall.
P3: The Size line and the reviewer's wc -c re-measure cost seconds per card, so the ceremony is light.
P4: Naming moved scope in the slice commit body, with a retro count of owned lines, guards against the cap pushing scope into follow-up cards.
P5: Deferring the mid-card review keeps this to one change per trial and adds no review window per card.
P6: The trial covers only the next 2 cards that would have been over the cap, so the line restarts soon and cards under the cap carry no overhead.
P7: Findings per card and slice-to-first-red (41 minutes) are measurable from git and the review records, and they are evidence, not targets.
P8: It is a two-way door: deleting the cap and the Size line changes no shared state.

P3: Re-measuring with `git show <commit>:<path> | wc -c` reads the committed blob, so line-ending conversion on checkout doesn't affect it, and a reviewer can run it mechanically. It is enforceable once P2 is pinned down.
P4: Naming each moved criterion in the commit body ("moved to card N") plus counting its owned lines in the retro is enough to watch the follow-up-card drift without a new file.
P5: Scoping the trial to the next 2 cards that would have had an oversize slice, with a keep/revise/drop retro, is bounded and reversible. The "No blur" rule keeps credit with the rule that named a finding first.
P6: The metrics and baseline are measurable from git and the review records, and they are described as evidence rather than targets, which fits the Goodhart guard.
